Title: Diagnosis of test `testCompareTo_otherEnumType`

Details:
The test `testCompareTo_otherEnumType` in `ValuedEnumTest` checks that comparing two enum instances of different types (`ValuedColorEnum.BLUE` and `ValuedLanguageEnum.ENGLISH`) using the `compareTo` method throws a `ClassCastException`. This is because these enums belong to different enum classes, so comparing them should not be allowed.

The method `compareTo` in `ValuedEnum` is defined as:
```java
public int compareTo(Object other) {
    return iValue - ((ValuedEnum) other).iValue;
}
```
This method casts the argument `other` to `ValuedEnum` and then performs a subtraction of their `iValue` fields. However, this cast does not verify that `other` is of the same subclass type as `this`. It only casts `other` to `ValuedEnum`. Since `ValuedColorEnum` and `ValuedLanguageEnum` are both subclasses of `ValuedEnum`, this cast to the parent class `ValuedEnum` will succeed regardless of the specific subclass. Therefore, no `ClassCastException` will be thrown by this cast.

As a result, the subtraction `iValue - ((ValuedEnum) other).iValue` executes without exception, returning an integer. This means the line in the test where `compareTo` is called with enums of different types does not throw a `ClassCastException` as expected, and instead no exception is thrown. Hence, the test fails because it expects a `ClassCastException`.

The root cause is that the `compareTo` method in `ValuedEnum` does not check whether `other` is an instance of the same enum subclass as `this` before performing the comparison. It only assumes `other` is a `ValuedEnum`, ignoring the subtype difference, so no exception is raised.

To fix this, `compareTo` should verify that `other` is of the same enum subclass as `this` (e.g., using `getClass()`) and throw a `ClassCastException` if they differ. This would enforce stricter type safety in comparisons, aligning with the test expectation.

Suggested methods to fix:
org.apache.commons.lang.enums.ValuedEnum.compareTo(java.lang.Object)
